newsitem.title: UK: Tin shows little scope to shine in 1997 - Billiton.
newsitem.headline: Tin shows little scope to shine in 1997 - Billiton.

text.p: Prospects for the tin market are not optimistic in 1997 as fundamentals are expected to retain last year's lacklustre tone, brokers Billiton said in a weekly report on Monday.

"The best that can be hoped for is a slight improvement in prices, but in our view the market may even struggle to do this, particularly if developments elsewhere in the complex (LME) are not conducive," the broker said.
Last year Western world refined metal production started to pick up, increasing around five percent for the year as a whole, after several years of decline.
Output is expected to continue rising in the year ahead, with Indonesia, Brazil and Peru forecast to see increased production, Billiton said.
The Western demand picture may be somewhat brighter in 1997 than last year's estimated year-on-year increase of just 0.6 percent.
However, Europe, the United States and Japan cannot be relied upon to provide impressive growth in base metal demand.

"...The South East Asian economies are likely to continue to be relied upon for growth impetus," Billiton said. "All the same we are not ruling out the fact that there is at least some scope for improvement."
Exports to the West from China will be an important factor, it said.
The latest customs figures show that exports of unwrought tin and tin alloys from China were 36,158 tonnes last year, a 16.5 percent decline from 1995's 43,307 tonnes.
"However, this has failed to inspire the market, because the perception is that producers in China have simply been holding off on exports in the hope of higher prices further ahead," Billiton said.

Chinese tin production appears set to extend last year's decline of 8.1 percent. But the general consensus is that exports would pick up significantly if values improved, thereby capping prices, Billiton said.
A big stockpile which is believed to have accumulated in 1994/1995 could offset any constraints in Chinese output, it added.
